behavior_items: The reproducer is a compile-time conformance test for the intrinsic module ISO_FORTRAN_ENV, not a runtime program.

Its essential source is `use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: INITIAL_TEAM, PARENT_TEAM, CURRENT_TEAM` followed by `end`, so the entire test is whether those names can be imported from the standard intrinsic module.
The `use, intrinsic` form forces the compiler to resolve `iso_fortran_env` as the standard intrinsic module rather than a user-provided module of the same name.

The `only:` clause narrows the import set to exactly three named entities: `INITIAL_TEAM`, `PARENT_TEAM`, and `CURRENT_TEAM`. This makes name lookup strict and directly tests whether each symbol exists in the module interface.
Under Fortran 2018, these three names are required named integer constants in ISO_FORTRAN_ENV because they are the valid `LEVEL` selector values for the `GET_TEAM()` intrinsic.

Therefore the compiler behavior being exercised is the front end's built-in definition and export list for ISO_FORTRAN_ENV, specifically whether it includes the new Fortran 2018 team-related constants.

No executable statements, declarations, or calls to `GET_TEAM()` are needed; successful compilation alone would prove that the compiler recognizes the constants and exposes them through module use association.
The observed failure occurs during semantic resolution of the USE statement: the compiler accepts the module name but reports that each requested symbol is not found in the intrinsic module.
The three diagnostics are independent missing-symbol errors, one for each constant, showing that the module exists but its symbol table lacks all three exports.

This distinguishes the bug from parser failure or module-loading failure: gfortran understands `use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env`, but its implementation of that intrinsic module is incomplete relative to the Fortran 2018 standard.
The reproducer specifically validates standard library/intrinsic-module completeness rather than code generation, optimization, or runtime library behavior.

Because the source uses only the import statement and an `end`, any rejection is attributable to compile-time intrinsic-module metadata, making the test minimal and sharply targeted at the missing constants bug.

The malformed `reproducer_code` field in the prompt appears to include report text around the actual test, but the bug report clearly identifies the intended reproducer as the one-line program importing the three constants from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV.

This shows the bug is not in parsing, runtime behavior, or `GET_TEAM()` execution, but in the compiler front end's incomplete implementation of the Fortran 2018 additions to `ISO_FORTRAN_ENV`.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern is a pure compile-time intrinsic-module conformance issue. The compiler successfully recognizes `use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env`, so module parsing and intrinsic-module selection work, but semantic lookup fails for all three requested names in the `only:` list. Because `INITIAL_TEAM`, `PARENT_TEAM`, and `CURRENT_TEAM` are required Fortran 2018 named integer constants exported by `ISO_FORTRAN_ENV` for use with `GET_TEAM()`, the common pattern is that gfortran's built-in definition of the intrinsic module is incomplete or not updated for the F2018 standard revision. The identical missing-symbol diagnostics for all three names strongly suggest a single front-end metadata/registration omission affecting the intrinsic module export table rather than unrelated parser, optimizer, or runtime defects.

If ref is not NULL, *ref is set to represent the chain of components required to get to the ultimate component.
